member.name: T:o2g.ICallCenterManagement
member.summary:
ICallCenterManagement provides operations to configure and manage CCD pilots and their associated calendars.
Usage of this service requires a CONTACTCENTER_SERVICE license in CAPEX mode, or 40 api-tel-f subscriptions in OPEX mode (Purple On Demand).
Each CCD pilot has two types of calendars:
Normal calendar — defines standard pilot behaviour for each day of the week. Each day can have up to 10 transitions (time slots).
Exceptional calendar — defines special days that override the normal calendar (e.g. holidays). Each exceptional day can also have up to 10 transitions.
A represents a time slot in a calendar, including the start time, the pilot rule to apply, and the pilot operating mode.

member.name: T:o2g.ICallCenterRealtime
member.summary: Provides real-time information about CCD objects from an OXE system in the form of events.
member.remarks:
This service is available only to administrators and delivers the same level of information as the legacy RTI interface available in the CCS.
The CCD objects that can be monitored include CCD agents, pilots, waiting queues, processing groups associated with agents, and other processing groups (e.g. forward, guide).
Typical usage sequence:
Build an specifying which objects and attributes to monitor.
Create an with the filter and the desired notification frequency.
Set the context with .
Register event handlers for the RTI events of interest.
Start monitoring with .
After initialization, the application is notified whenever one or more monitored attributes change. Each event contains only the attributes that have changed since the previous notification.
Access to this service requires a valid license: CONTACTCENTER_SERVICE in CAPEX mode, or 40 api-tel-f subscriptions in OPEX mode (Purple On Demand).

member.name: T:o2g.ICallCenterStatistics
member.summary: Provides access to OmniPCX Enterprise call-center statistics for CCD agents and pilots.
member.remarks:
This service supports two modes of data retrieval:
Immediate reports — statistics retrieved on demand, returned as in-memory data or exported as CSV or Excel files.
Scheduled reports — recurring statistics delivered as email attachments to predefined recipients.
Statistics are accessed through a two-level hierarchy:
A defines the scope of agents whose data can be accessed.
A defines the filter criteria (pilots, agents, queues) for which statistics are collected.
The typical usage sequence is:
Create a requester with , specifying the agents in scope.
Create a context with , specifying the filter criteria.
Retrieve data with for a single day, or for a date range.
Delete the context and requester when done.
Using this service requires a CONTACTCENTER_SERVICE license in CAPEX mode, or a 40 api-tel-f subscription in OPEX mode (Purple On Demand).

member.summary: Asynchronously downloads statistics for a single day as a report file.

remarks.para: The server generates the file asynchronously and delivers the result as a ZIP archive. The single entry within the archive is extracted into . The returned task completes when the extracted file has been saved to disk.
Statistics are reported in time slots defined by , spanning from 00:00 until the last completed interval of the specified day. When is , no time-slot breakdown is applied.

Only one asynchronous report generation request can be active at a time. Any attempt to start another request while one is already in progress will cause the returned task to fault with an InvalidOperationException. Use to abort an in-progress request.

member.param: The statistics context defining the scope and filters.
The day for which to generate the report.
The slot granularity; for a single daily aggregate.
The destination directory. The extracted file is placed inside this directory. When , the system Downloads folder is used.

member.summary: Retrieves the next available results for the current search.
member.returns: A object in case of success; otherwise.

remarks.para:
is generally called in a loop. For each iteration:
If the result code is Nok the search is in progress but no results are available yet — it is recommended to wait before the next iteration (e.g., 500 ms).
If the result code is Ok results are available and can be processed.
If the result code is Finish or TimeOut the search has ended — exit the loop.

member.name: T:o2g.IPbxManagement
member.summary: IPbxManagement allows an administrator to manage an OmniPCX Enterprise, that is to create, modify or delete any object or sub-object in the OmniPCX Enterprise object model. Using this service requires having a MANAGEMENT license.

remarks.para: WARNING: Using this service requires a good knowledge of the OmniPCX Enterprise object model.

The service uses two kinds of resource: the object model resource and the object instance resource.
The object model resource The object model can be retrieved for the whole PBX or for a particular object. It provides the detail of object attributes: whether the attribute is mandatory or optional in the object creation, what range of values is authorized, and what the possible enumeration values are.
The object instance resource It is used to create, modify, retrieve or remove any instances of any object, given the reference of this object. For the creation or modification of an object, the body must be compliant with the object model.

The list of sub-objects returned by a get instance of an object corresponds to the relative path of the first instantiable objects in the hierarchy, in order to be able by recursion to build the path to access any object and sub-object.
When accessing an object which is a sub-object, the full path must be given: {object1Name}/{object1Id}/{object2Name}/{object2Id}/.../{objectxName}/{objectxId}.

member.name: T:o2g.IRecording
member.summary: The ROD OXR Recording service allows starting, pausing, or resuming voice recording of an OXE device on one or more OXR recorders.
member.remarks:
All necessary permissions must be configured on the OXR side for the dedicated user to perform start/pause/resume operations.
If a device is configured in multiple OXRs, the request is sent to all relevant OXRs. A successful action on any one OXR is considered a success for the overall request.
Modifications on an OXR may require a restart of the OXR service. To apply such changes immediately, O2G services must also be restarted; otherwise, the O2G server refreshes automatically after a scheduled period (4 hours). After a new device is created on an OXR, the O2G server is refreshed automatically for that device.
This service does not provide real-time notifications of changes in recording state caused by call evolutions (e.g., hold, retrieve, transfer, conference, intrusion). Applications may deduce the recording state using call monitoring.
Only two telephony call states are relevant for recording actions:
HELD: If a call was recording before hold, the recording state is memorized and actions are disabled.
ACTIVE:
New call without recording: "start" action possible.
Call from transfer/conference: recording stopped, new "start" action possible.
Hold retrieve: recording resumes previous state.
Other cases: no change.
While the API allows inferring recording state from telephony events, it is recommended to query the device to get the updated recording state. Typical event-to-state mappings:
ACTIVE -> HELD: recording stalled, no action possible
ACTIVE caused by TRANSFERRED/CONFERENCE: no recording in progress, "start" possible
HELD -> ACTIVE (not TRANSFERRED/CONFERENCE): previous recording resumes
ACTIVE -> ACTIVE (not TRANSFERRED/CONFERENCE): no change
Other -> ACTIVE (not TRANSFERRED/CONFERENCE): new "start" possible
New callref with state=ACTIVE: new "start" possible
Since version 2.7.3

member.name: T:o2g.IRouting
member.summary:
Provides operations to manage a user's call routing configuration, including forward, overflow, Do Not Disturb, and remote extension activation.
Using this service requires a TELEPHONY_ADVANCED license.
Forward — redirects incoming calls to the user's voice mail or to another phone number, subject to an optional . A number must be authorized by the OmniPCX Enterprise numbering policy. Use or to activate, and to cancel.
Overflow — redirects incoming calls to the user's voice mail when a specified is met. Unlike a forward, an overflow only applies when no forward is active. Use to activate, and to cancel.
Do Not Disturb — when active, no calls are presented to the user. Use to activate and to cancel.
Remote extension — when a remote extension (e.g. a mobile device) is deactivated, it does not ring on incoming calls but can still place outgoing calls. Use to activate and to deactivate.
member.remarks: For all methods, if the session has been opened for a user the loginName parameter is ignored. It is mandatory only when the session has been opened by an administrator acting on behalf of a specific user.

member.name: T:o2g.IUserManagement
member.summary:
The IUserManagement service allows an administrator to create, delete, and retrieve O2G users. O2G allows users to be created according to different methods:
Automatically when O2G starts, according to the automatic user creation mode.
Through provisioning files.
On demand through this service, which allows creating one user, a list of users, or all users on a given OmniPCX Enterprise node.
Using this service does not require any specific license on the O2G server.

member.summary:
The IUsers service allows:
An administrator to retrieve the list of O2G users.
A user to get information on another user account.
A user to change their password or get parameters such as supported languages.
Using this service does not require any specific license on the O2G server.

member.name: T:o2g.IWebHook
member.summary: Represents a Webhook configuration used for receiving O2G events.

remarks.para: When eventing is configured via a Webhook, the application must expose an HTTP endpoint and provide its URL to the SDK through this interface.
Once the subscription is successfully established, the SDK invokes to supply an instance. The application is then responsible for forwarding incoming HTTP POST request bodies to this processor.

member.value: A containing the Webhook endpoint URL that the O2G server will use to POST events.

member.summary: Called by the SDK when the event subscription is established.
member.param: The that the application must call for each HTTP POST body received at its Webhook endpoint.
member.remarks: The application should store the provided and invoke inside its HTTP endpoint handler for every incoming event POST.

member.name: T:o2g.Subscription
member.summary:
Subscription represents a subscription request used to subscribe events from the O2G Server.
The application builds a subscription using the object. This object provides a builder pattern that eases the creation of a subscription.
member.example:
To create a subscription, uses the methods provided by the Builder object.
Subscription subscription = Subscription.Builder .AddRoutingEvents() // Add routing service events .AddTelephonyEvents() // Add telephony service events .AddEventSummaryEvents() // Add event summary events .SetTimeout(10) // Set the chunk connection timeout .Build(); // Build the subscription

member.returns: The this event package has been added to.

member.summary: Add the specified eventPackage to the subscription.
member.returns: The this event package has been added to.

member.summary: Return the version of the events to subscribe to.
member.value: A value that represents the events version.
member.remarks: By default the event version is "1.0".

member.name: P:o2g.Subscription.Timeout
member.summary: Return the default lifetime of the event channel.
member.value: A value that represents the events channel lifetime in minute.

remarks.para: When chunk eventing is used, the server closes the connection in case of no activity after the timeout. In this case, the event channel is automatically re-established.

Allowed values are 2 minutes and 60 minutes, with an exception for the value 0. For this special case, the lifetime of the notification channel is not maintained by the given timeout, but depends on the lifetime of the user's session. A KeepAlive event is sent by the server to maintain the connection.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.CallCenterRealtimeNS.RtiObjectIdentifier
member.summary:
Represents a CCD object identifier for which real-time information is available.
Instances of this class provide details about a CCD object, such as agents, pilots, or queues, that can be monitored using the CallCenterRealtime.
Each object includes a directory number, last name, first name, and a unique key. This class is typically used to retrieve and reference objects for real-time events.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.CommunicationLogNS.ComRecordParticipant
member.summary: ComRecordParticipant represents a participant referenced in a com record.

remarks.para:
For a simple call (user A calls user B), the call record on each party will contain both the participant A and the participant B: (no guaranty on the order of the participants on 2 successive responses).
SideCom record content
On A side
Participant A (the owner of the record) with role=Caller and the answered status (whether the call has been answered or not)
Participant B : neither the role nor the state is provided
On B side
Participant A : neither the role nor the state is provided
Participant B (the owner of the record) with role=Callee and the answered status (whether the call has been answered or not)

For a re-routed call (user A calls user B, the call is re-routed on user C, caused by overflow, redirection or pickup), the record generated on each side including the user B side (the "victim" of the re-routing) will not contain as participant the user B itself because he was not the last destination of the call:
SideCom record content
On A side
Participant A : with role=Caller, the answered status, initialCalled=B
Participant C
On B side
Participant A : neither the role nor the state is provided
Participant C with role=Callee, the answered status (whether the call has been answered or not) and initialCalled=B which tells B that he was called by A but the call has been rerouted to C(with a reason) which answered or not to the call
On C side
Participant A : neither the role nor the state is provided
Participant C with role=Callee, the answered status (whether the call has been answered or not) and initialCalled=B

Furthermore, for a multi-parties call using addParticipant, the already connected users in the call will also received a call record which will contain the answered status of the added participant: this information is provided to distinguish the added participants which have really answered and the other which decline the call.

In the comlog notification events, the participant owner is identified only by its loginName (in order to reduce the event call flow), the other participants are identified with their full identity (loginName, phoneNumber).

In a result:
if no optimization is asked, all the participants are identified with their full identity.
If the optimized parameter is set to , only the first occurence of a participant (owner or other) is identified with its full identity. The following occurences are identified only with the phonenumber.

member.summary: EventSummary represents event counters associated to the user. It allows a user to get its new message indicators (missed call, voice mails, callback request, fax).

member.name: P:o2g.Types.EventSummaryNS.EventSummary.MissedCallsNb
member.summary: Return the number of missed calls.
member.value: A optional value that gives the number of missed calls.

remarks.para: If this attribute is not specified, it means that the server is not able to provide that information.

CAUTION: This attribute doesn't reflect the missed call number managed by the call server itself but is related to the unanswered and non acknowledged incoming calls in the history call. Therefore, either only the explicit acknowledgment of these history com records through the communication log API service, or a new answered call with the same user will decrease this counter. Moreover, the counter is incremented for each non answered incoming call, including successive attempts from the same caller.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.Host
member.summary:
This class represents an O2G host.
An O2G host can be reacheable from the local network, or from a wide area network. In this case, enterprise access can be secured by a reverse proxy border element.
An O2G host as a private address which is the IP address or the URI used to reach the O2G server on a local network, and a public address which is the IP address or the URI used to reach the O2G server through a reverse proxy.
member.remarks: It's possible to have only one address configured, but an exception will be throws if both are .

member.value: The private IP address of URI, or if the private address is not defined.

member.name: P:o2g.Types.Host.PublicAddress
member.summary: This property is the public address of this host.
member.value: The public IP address of URI, or if the public address is not defined.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.ManagementNS.PbxAttribute
member.summary:
PbxAttribute class represents an attribute in a .
A PbxAttribute can be of the following type:
Integer An Integer value is equivalent to an value.
Boolean A Boolean value is equivalent to an value.
Enumerated An enumerated value can have a limited set of possible values. PbxAttribute treats enumerated value as value.
OctetString, ByteString An OctetString or a ByteString are equivalent to a .
Sequence A Sequence is a structured data whose attribute member have a specific name and type: For exemple
Skill := Sequence { Skill_Nb := Integer, Skill_Level := Integer, Skill_Activate := Boolean }
Set A Set value is a list of attributes of the same type. It can be a list of simple value like:
SimpleSet := Set { Item := OctetString }
or a list of sequences:
SkillSet := Set { Item := Sequence { Skill_Nb := Integer, Skill_Level := Integer, Skill_Activate := Boolean } }

remarks.para: PbxAttribute provide conversion method to usual C# types. The conversion is controlled "at the best", but it can not check all the possible error case. An Enumerated value and an OctetString value can both be converted to a .
When a conversion error is detected, a exception is raised.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.PhoneSetProgrammingNS.Pin
member.summary: Pin class represents a PIN (Personal Identification Number)

remarks.para: This service allows the user to announce that the call he is making is a personal (external) call and not a business call. Using pulse metering tickets, the company is then able to invoice this call again as a personal call.
This service can be applied to local users (employees) or visitors (in this case, the created user set is a virtual set without a physical address).
To use this service, users must dial the personal prefix followed by the PIN No. and then the secret code followed by the external number.
The Personal Identification Number is private and secret; only the administrator and, in certain cases, the pulse metering administrator may know it.

member.summary: The routing service has rejected the request for a bad or missing parameter reason.

member.name: F:o2g.Types.RestErrorInfo.RoutingErrorInfo.RoutingErrorType.Unauthorized
member.summary:
Routing service request has been rejected because of limitation configured on the concerned user. For examples:
Overflow on busy is not allowed (barring limitation).
Cancel overflow is not allowed: (barring limitation).
Phone number to other destination is not authorized (dial plan limitation).

member.name: F:o2g.Types.RestErrorInfo.RoutingErrorInfo.RoutingErrorType.InvalidOperation
member.summary: Requested operation is not supported by the routing service.

member.name: F:o2g.Types.RestErrorInfo.RoutingErrorInfo.RoutingErrorType.IncompletePhoneNumber
member.summary:
The provided phone number can not be fully resolved in the current dial plan. For example:
Setting route with a destination type Other, containing a partially matching number (e.g. 3253 instead of 32535).

member.name: F:o2g.Types.RestErrorInfo.RoutingErrorInfo.RoutingErrorType.UnknownPhoneNumber
member.summary:
The provided phone number can not be resolved in the current dial plan. For example:
Setting route with a destination type NUMBER, containing an unknown number.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.RoutingNS.RoutingState
member.summary:
Represents the complete routing state of a user.
The routing state aggregates four independent routing features:
FeatureDescription
Remote extension
When configured, a remote extension (e.g. a mobile device) can be activated or deactivated. When deactivated, the device does not ring on incoming calls but can still be used to place outgoing calls.
Forward
Redirects incoming calls to the user's voice mail or to another number, subject to an optional condition. Takes priority over overflow.
Overflow
Redirects incoming calls to the user's voice mail when the user is busy or does not answer. Only applies when no forward is active.
Do Not Disturb
When active, no calls are presented to the user.

member.value: A object describing the active forward, or a with if no forward is configured.

member.summary: The overflow currently configured for the user.
member.value: An object describing the active overflow, or an with if no overflow is configured.

member.name: T:o2g.Types.TelephonyNS.CorrelatorData
member.summary:
Represents correlator data attached to a call.
Correlator data is application-provided information (limited to 32 bytes) that travels with a call. It is typically used to carry application context from one party to another across telephony operations such as transfer.
For example, user A receives an external call and attaches correlator data to it. When user A transfers the call to user B, user B receives an call created event whose contains the same correlator data, allowing user B's application to retrieve the original context.

member.returns: A representation of the correlator data.
